nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox testing costs
Legacy Oracle data extraction tooling / temp DB hosting

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog sizing and rate card only.

Story points roughly mapped to effort using a ~6-7 hours/point baseline for backend-heavy tasks, adjusted by role split per task type (e.g. UI-heavy tasks skew Frontend, data migration skews Backend+DevOps).
1 point ~= 1 ideal day of combined effort; total backlog points (81) translated into role hours based on FTE availability and task nature.

QA Engineer is only 0.6 FTE (~24 hrs/week) against 8 backlog tasks needing test coverage; 200 hours allocated is proportionate but represents a tight allocation - QA is likely a bottleneck, especially for PW-3, PW-4, PW-7 (auth, permissions, payments) which are high-risk areas needing thorough testing.

DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (~16 hrs/week); 90 hours covers CI/staging setup (PW-1) plus support for data migration cutover (PW-8) and Stripe webhook infra (PW-7), but is thinly staffed relative to the backlog - flagged as a risk.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) is assumed to require significant Backend Developer time for ETL scripts plus DevOps support for environment/hosting; no legacy schema documentation assumed available, which could increase actual effort.
PW-7 (Payment provider integration) assumes use of Stripe's standard hosted APIs/webhooks rather than a custom PCI-scope solution.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for cloud infra, Stripe sandbox usage, and temporary migration tooling/hosting; actual vendor quotes not yet available.
Estimate assumes a single delivery team working sequentially/in parallel within the stated FTE constraints, not multiple parallel squads.

Pessimistic scenario accounts for risk of legacy data migration complexity (undocumented schema, data quality issues) and payment reconciliation edge cases; optimistic scenario assumes clean legacy data and no major integration surprises.
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 81 story points across 8 tasks. Hours were allocated per task based on typical effort distribution across the four available roles, then rolled up: Backend Developer 520h, Frontend Developer 360h, QA Engineer 200h, DevOps Engineer 90h, for a total labour cost of $107,431.60. Non-labour costs of $4,800 cover Stripe sandbox fees, legacy DB extraction tooling, and initial staging/CI infrastructure, bringing the Most Likely total to $112,231.60. This matches the 50th percentile scenario. The Optimistic (10th percentile, $100,000) scenario assumes minimal rework and clean legacy data; the Pessimistic (90th percentile, $135,000) scenario adds ~20% contingency for known risk areas: legacy data migration (PW-8) and payment integration (PW-7), plus the thin staffing on QA and DevOps roles relative to backlog size. Priority breakdown allocates cost proportionally to task priority: Urgent tasks (PW-3, PW-7) drive $39,500, High priority tasks (PW-1, PW-4, PW-5, PW-8) drive $51,500, and Medium priority tasks (PW-2, PW-6) drive $21,231.60. No historical actuals exist for this project, so all effort estimates are derived from backlog sizing and reasonable role-based effort splits rather than empirical data.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal token/theme set now, deferring full component library (buttons/forms/tables/dialogs) to a post-launch phase.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~100h; core screens use basic unstyled components initially, full design system delivered in a later iteration.

reductions.description: Defer PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view) to a follow-up release, launching first with dashboard and payments only.
reductions.effect: Removes ~80h Backend + ~30h Frontend + ~10h QA tied to this Medium-priority feature from the initial delivery scope.

reductions.description: Reduce DevOps scope on PW-8 by using a phased/batched migration script run during off-hours instead of building fully automated zero-downtime tooling.
reductions.effect: Cuts DevOps hours on migration support from ~30h to ~0h by relying on Backend-led scripted batch migration with a short maintenance window.

reductions.description: Use Stripe Checkout (hosted page) instead of custom card-entry UI for PW-7, reducing Frontend and Backend integration effort.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~30h Backend and ~20h Frontend from payment integration by offloading PCI scope and UI to Stripe-hosted flow.

reductions.description: Defer non-critical staging environment enhancements and use a shared low-cost cloud tier for the first 3 months.
reductions.effect: Reduces staging/CI infrastructure non-labour spend from $1,800 to ~$800 by using smaller instance sizes until traffic grows.
